chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Al-Fadl Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the Statement of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'Or who come to you, their hearts shrinking from fighting you or fighting their own people' — he said: 'It was revealed concerning the Banu Mudlaj, because they came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'Indeed, our chests are restricted from testifying that you are the Messenger of Allah, so we are not with you, nor are we with our people against you.' I said: 'How did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) deal with them?' He said: 'He made an appointment with them until he was free from the Arabs, then he would call them; if they answered, [well and good], otherwise he would fight them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the occasion of revelation for the verse 'Or who come to you, their hearts shrinking from fighting you or fighting their own people'?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the specific historical context (shay'an al-nuzul) of Quran 4:90, identifying the Banu Mudlaj tribe as the subjects whose 'hearts were restricted' by tribal loyalties. It highlights the Prophet's strategic patience (hilm), delaying their judgment until the consolidation of power against other Arab tribes, thereby offering them a clear choice between acceptance of Islam or combat, a nuance crucial for understanding the flexibility of early Islamic jurisprudence.
